title: fix(plugin-security): a sharing allow keeps the ownership floor beside an authored write policy, so a creator writes their own row by id
body:
Fixes #35917

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化:业务对象上配了「满足条件可改/删」规则时,创建人按单条记录改或删自己建的记录不再被误拒,和批量改的结果一致。
- 为什么做:修复「按单条改」与「批量改」对同一条记录给出相反答案的问题,按你已拍板的「放行」方案落地。
- 出错会怎样:最坏情况是创建人能改删一条本该被规则拦住的自己的记录;改动只在服务端权限判断里,撤回这个合并即可恢复。
- 要你做什么:无。

## What changes

The maintainer ruled option A on #35917 (ruling comment 7063130499; the analysis is comment 7062795693): under a record sharing `allow`, the platform ownership floor (`created_by == current_user.id`) stays an OR term beside an app-authored update or delete `using` policy. It is dropped only where it is the OR's last term.

- **Pre-image row gate** (`computeLayeredRlsFilter`, `security-plugin-rls-filter.ts`). With `dropPlatformOwnershipFloor`, the floor leaves Layer 1 only when the policies left after it carry no `using` term (asked through the same field-existence pass the compile uses). Beside an authored `using` it stays.
- **Post-image check** (`computeWriteCheckFilter`, same file). The defaulted check keeps the floor term on the same condition, so the stored row is judged by the same OR. A `check` an author wrote still refuses.
- **Authored probe** (`checkAuthoredRowWrite`, `security-plugin-authored-row-write.ts`). It now takes the floor out of the permission SETS by provenance instead of through the knob, so it still judges the authored policies alone and still answers `abstain` where no authored policy matches.
- Every caller of `dropPlatformOwnershipFloor` gets the one meaning: the step 2.7 by-id gate, the predicate path's relief (`predicateWriteFloorRelief`, comments only: its `floored OR id IN dropIds` now agrees with the by-id answer), the `controlled_by_parent` master check, the delegator's own composition (`delegatorOwnWriteFloorOptions`) and `security/explain`. The authored probe is the one caller that no longer uses the knob, for the reason above.
- The claim's surface was amended to cover `security-plugin.ts`, so these edits are no longer a breach:
  - the `RlsFilterOptions.dropPlatformOwnershipFloor` jsdoc line;
  - N1: the `checkAuthoredRowWrite` docblock no longer says the probe is driven by the knob;
  - the L1-a item: `writeCheckPolicies` point 3 now says the floor stays in the check beside an authored `using` under an `allow`, and names the pass-1 corner where the check keeps a floor the pre-image dropped.
- **Docs and changeset (S2, S3, N2):**
  - `permissions-matrix.mdx` now agrees with `sharing-rules.mdx`: both paths keep the floor beside an authored `using`.
  - `rls.mdx` says a write policy is one more OR term that adds rows, names the cbp exception, and says where a cap goes.
  - The changeset and `sharing-rules.mdx` now:
    - drop "a creator who does not own the row is still refused": write depth, Modify All, an `edit` share or a queue earn `allow`;
    - scope "by id and by predicate agree" to the rows the floor admits and name the divergence;
    - say a `check` bounds only the stored image, and name a `beforeUpdate` hook reading `ctx.previous` for the prior state, `beforeDelete` for a delete, and a hook on the detail object for a master's details;
    - state the master-gate consequence;
    - name the lifecycle verbs (`transfer` with update, `purge` with delete; `restore` addresses no single row id and does not meet the gate) and the fail-closed outcome that moves.
  - N3 and N5 are left, as directed.

**Removed capability.** A `using` write policy no longer stops a row's own creator once record sharing says `allow`, and the same holds for a `controlled_by_parent` master's creator writing its details beside the master's authored update policy. A `check` bounds only the stored image of an update; a limit on the prior state goes in a `beforeUpdate` hook reading `ctx.previous`, a delete's limit in a `beforeDelete` hook, and a limit on a master's details in a hook on the detail object.

**Fixture changes (the ruling turns 22 pinned refusals into admissions).** The #24746 / ADR-0090 D10 fixtures pinned the old refusal on rows the delegator created. Each test keeps its invariant and every assertion exactly as written; only the rows moved:

- `delegated-write-never-exceeds-delegator.test.ts` (12 tests: five held-row cells and the post-image store test, under both tenancy postures). `held_1`, `held_del_direct`, `held_del_agent`, `store_direct`, `store_agent` and the master `m_held` are now created by OTHER (owner still BOUNDED); `held_2` is owned and created by OTHER. New rows `held_created`, `held_created_del_direct`, `held_created_del_agent` (owned and created by BOUNDED) back two new cells, update and delete: a held row the delegator created is admitted for the delegator and on its behalf.
- `explain-enforce-parity.test.ts` (10 tests: five #24746 rows under both postures). `p_bounded_held`, `p_del_bounded_held` and `m_bounded_held` are now created by D_OTHER. New row `p_bounded_held_created` backs two new '#35917' table rows, agent and direct update, both admitted, with explain equal to enforce.

## Why

On an object where an authored update or delete policy applied (for example "any open deal"), a sharing `allow` deleted the floor term from the OR, so the creator-owner's own closed row was refused by id with 403 while a predicate write over the same row wrote it. By id and by predicate now give one answer on the rows the floor admits (the open-row divergence on rows it does not admit is tracked on #35934).

## Tests

New describe in `predicate-write-floor-deferral.test.ts`, `[#35917] beside an authored widener ...`, extending the #35914 matrix with the widener:

| Caller (all rows closed unless named) | By id | Predicate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ALICE, owner-creator, her closed r1, update and delete | admitted (was 403, the defect) | admitted (agrees) |
| ALICE with r2 open | r1 by the floor, r2 by the widener | the same rows |
| BOB, owner who created none | nothing, as before | nothing |
| CAROL, creator who owns none | nothing: the floor admits, record sharing does not | nothing |
| Modify All holder, rows it did not create | nothing, unchanged (ADR-0066 ①) | nothing |
| Modify All holder, open r2 and r3 | r2, r3, unchanged | r2, r3 |
| Modify All holder, a closed row it created | admitted by the floor | admitted |
| DAVE, edit-share target on closed rows | nothing | nothing |
| DAVE, closed shared r2 he created (N4) | update admitted by the floor; delete refused (ADR-0111 D3) | the same |
| DAVE, update with r2 open, shared to him | r2, not the closed r3 | the same |

CONTROLS: an authored EMEA `check` still refuses ALICE's closed r1 moved out of EMEA (403 PERMISSION_DENIED); the tenant wall still refuses her own row in another organization; on an owner-less object (sharing abstains) the floor still applies (r1, r3 only). `security/explain` answers the verdict the write gets.

Also pinned (N4):

- The edit-share target DAVE who created the closed shared r2, under the wideners. The update is admitted by the floor, by id and by predicate. The delete is still refused (ADR-0111 D3). A1 turns the update red.

Ablations (each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on the committed fix, restore proven by an empty `git diff HEAD`):

- A1, pre-image keeps deleting the floor term: pin file 8 failed / 49; rewritten D10 + parity files 8 failed / 192 (all four new `held_created` cells and all four new parity rows).
- A2, post-image check keeps deleting the floor term: pin file 4 failed / 49.
- A3, authored probe composes with the floor in its sets: pin file 7 failed / 49; `authored-row-write-verdict.test.ts` 1 failed (the abstain pin for a creator whose authored policy does not match).

Full plugin-security suite and typecheck at the head: see Verification.

## Acceptance notes

- **The #24792 delegator-own guard is pinned where it still narrows.** On an ordinary object, ruling A makes the delegator's own composition a superset of the floor-kept delegator filter the delegated path already ANDs, so the guard narrows nothing there. It still narrows on a `controlled_by_parent` object. There the delegator's direct write carries the master-gate vouch, so the floor yields and the delegator's authored detail policy decides alone, while every floor-standing filter on the delegated path admits a row the delegator created. The body's earlier "an OWD that opens row writes" was wrong: `platformFloorYieldsToObjectWriteModel` answers for `public_read_write` from the object alone, so both delegator filters drop the floor there and the guard narrows nothing. The D10 rig gets the authored update policy `note != 'held'` on its cbp DETAIL, a grand detail whose master is DETAIL (DETAIL becomes a middle master), and three pins, each under both postures:
  - by-id update of `d_note_held` (the step 2.7 site);
  - the store test on `d_store_*` (the post-image check site);
  - update of `g_under_mid_held` under the held middle master (the master-gate site).

  Each pin refuses both the delegator's own write and the write on its behalf, and explain agrees for the two cells. Ablation on the D10, parity and pin files (253 tests), each through `ablation-replace.mjs`, restore proven by `git diff HEAD` = 0 lines:
  - G1 (`delOwnWriteFilter` removed): 2 red, the step 2.7 cell under both postures;
  - G2 (`delOwnCheckFilter` removed): 2 red, the detail store test under both postures;
  - G3 (`delegatorOwnMasterWriteFilter` removed): 2 red, the middle-master cell under both postures.
- **Open-row by-id vs predicate divergence (held finding, not fixed here).** Under an authored write widener, an OPEN row the caller neither owns nor holds a share on is admitted by id (the authored probe lifts the sharing refusal) but left out of a predicate write (the sharing bulk scope stays owner and shares). The relief test in `predicate-write-floor-deferral.test.ts` records it: by id r1, r2, r3, r4; by predicate r1, r2. Tracked on #35934 (comment 7065565832): it is that card's predicate bulk write scope, in the same files, so it was folded there rather than filed apart. `Fixes #35917` still holds: ruling A (7063130499) asks for one answer on the rows the platform floor admits, and this divergence is on rows the floor does not admit.
- The #35802 relief test in `predicate-write-floor-deferral.test.ts` now pins the by-id answer r1, r2, r3, r4 against the predicate's r1, r2. That locks the held out-of-scope finding (a), the open-row by-id vs predicate divergence, in place until that finding is worked.
- #35934 proceeds on its own premise and is out of scope here.
- The `controlled_by_parent` half of #35802 is out of scope here.
- **S4, the master check's widening is pinned.** The D10 rig gets the master `m_held_created`: held, owned and created by the delegator. Under it are the details `d_under_held_created` and `d_under_held_created_del_direct` / `_agent`. A detail update and a detail delete are both admitted for the delegator and on its behalf, with explain agreeing, under both postures. A1 turns all 4 red.

## Verification

- Head `a82a0b1be0` for every run below. Head `1b90fa5f2a` (seat 4, contract record 7065591342 NEW-1/NEW-2/NEW-4) changes only `rls.mdx` prose and one changeset sentence.
- Full plugin-security suite: VERDICT command-exit 0. Test Files 286 passed (286); Tests 7151 passed, 45 skipped (7196).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck`: VERDICT command-exit 0.
- dispatch-gates at `a82a0b1be0` derived 104 families: 101 exit 0. `--ran` reconciliation: 104 accounted, 101 run, 3 NOT MEASURED, 0 unrun.
- The three NOT MEASURED exited 3 with PREREQUISITE NOT MET. CI runs them:
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:skill-examples`
  - `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`
  - `pnpm check:i18n`
- `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 36117`: NOT governed. 0 of 11 paths hit the register; 594 changed lines.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/predicate-write-floor-deferral.test.ts` prints every test passed, including the `[#35917] beside an authored widener` describe.

Read first: (1) `security-plugin-rls-filter.ts`, the `withoutFloor` hunk in `computeLayeredRlsFilter`, the decision itself; (2) the `floorReplaced` hunk in `computeWriteCheckFilter`, which must agree with (1); (3) `security-plugin-authored-row-write.ts`, the probe that must not start answering `admit`.

- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: not touched.
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
